facts.fact: Adwave's guide page was published on 2026-08-09.
Adwave recommends structuring a 30-second mobile app promo as a hook at 0 to 3 seconds.
facts.quote: **Hook, 0 to 3 seconds.** Show the app’s promise or the pain point immediately.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends a problem beat at 3 to 8 seconds in a 30-second mobile app promo.
facts.quote: **Problem, 3 to 8 seconds.** Make the need feel real and specific.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends an in-app proof beat at 8 to 22 seconds in a 30-second mobile app promo.
facts.quote: **In-app proof, 8 to 22 seconds.** Show the interface or service flow doing the job.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends a call-to-action beat at 22 to 30 seconds in a 30-second mobile app promo.
facts.quote: **CTA, 22 to 30 seconds.** Tell viewers what to do next and where to go.

facts.fact: Adwave lists the App Store preview duration as 15 to 30 seconds, with landscape orientation recommended.
facts.quote: | App Store preview | 15 to 30 seconds | Landscape recommended |

facts.fact: Adwave states that the practical target for a Google Play video is around 30 seconds to under 2 minutes, and that Google Play uses a YouTube video link.
facts.quote: Google Play is looser on upload mechanics because it uses a **YouTube video link**, but the practical target is still a compact spot, usually around **30 seconds to under 2 minutes**.

facts.fact: Adwave lists 9:16 as the aspect ratio for Meta and TikTok paid social placements.
facts.quote: | Meta and TikTok paid social | Short hook-led cuts | 9:16 |

facts.fact: Adwave lists 16:9 as the aspect ratio for CTV and broadcast placements.
facts.quote: | CTV and broadcast | Varies by buy | 16:9 |

facts.fact: Adwave states that App Store guidance limits non-in-app content to no more than 20% of the preview video.
facts.quote: it limits non-in-app content to **no more than 20%** of the video

facts.fact: Adwave says its campaigns can run across 100+ premium channels.
facts.quote: the campaign can run across **100+ premium channels** with campaigns starting at **$30 a day**

facts.fact: Adwave says campaigns start at $30 a day.
facts.quote: campaigns starting at **$30 a day** and automatic pacing

facts.fact: The page recommends editing a 30-second master video first, then deriving social and broadcast or CTV cutdowns from it.
The page's launch-day checklist contains ten items.
facts.quote: **Review notes logged** so the next edit starts smarter.

facts.fact: The page includes a diagram showing five metrics for tracking mobile application marketing performance, titled The Install Measurement Ladder.
facts.quote: A diagram titled The Install Measurement Ladder showing five metrics for tracking mobile application marketing performance.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its workflow can generate a broadcast-ready spot for TV distribution alongside mobile assets from a URL or brief.
facts.quote: because it can generate a broadcast-ready spot for TV distribution alongside mobile assets

facts.fact: Adwave describes its process as entering a URL and then generating a polished spot for distribution as a fast layer for SMBs.
facts.quote: You enter a URL, it generates a polished spot, and the campaign can run across

facts.fact: The page states that on mobile, a large share of viewing happens without sound, so captions are part of the deliverable.
facts.quote: On mobile, a large share of viewing happens without sound, so the caption track is part of the deliverable
